post.summary:
Starts a new conversation, optionally bound to a Ticket or a Cantiere (never
    both). The row-scope permission check below runs BEFORE the session is created — the same
    permission the orchestrator's own `get_current_ticket`/`get_current_cantiere`

Resolves the conversation's draft against real tenant data and returns it — the terminal
action of a copilot session. It creates nothing: no `Report`, no Bozza, no attachment
association, no report-lifecycle side effect, and no report id for a caller to depend on
(spec §5.4). The pre-flight (IAiDraftPreflight) still runs, so a reference that
no longer resolves is a 422 on the draft rather than a half-written report; nothing in this
path writes.

The session deliberately survives a successful resolve. Confirming is now safe to repeat —
two calls return the same draft — and a caller that loses the response can retry and recover
it, which a delete-on-success made impossible. The session is released by
Task<IActionResult> AiConversationsController.Abandon(Guid id, CancellationToken ct) instead, once the caller has actually persisted the draft.

post.summary: Start cantiere work (arrive at site).

Batch-starts cantiere clock-in for multiple teammates at once. Restricted to a caller
who is themselves assigned to this cantiere as lead (bool CantiereCrewAssignment.IsLead)
— a non-lead uses Task<IActionResult> CantiereWorkLogController.StartWork(StartCantiereWorkLogRequest request, CancellationToken ct) for their own clock-in and cannot batch-start
for anyone else through this endpoint, including themselves.
post.description:
Per-person, not all-or-nothing: an already-open shift or a userId not assigned to this
cantiere names that person as a failure in the response (mirroring
`RolePermissionMatrixService.SetMatrixAsync`'s "name every offender" pattern) rather
than either silently dropping them or failing the whole batch for everyone else.

post.summary: Idempotent batch upsert of cantiere punches captured on a device.
post.description:
The offline counterpart to Task<IActionResult> CantiereWorkLogController.StartWork(StartCantiereWorkLogRequest request, CancellationToken ct)/Task<IActionResult> CantiereWorkLogController.EndWork(EndCantiereWorkLogRequest? request = null), mirroring
`POST /api/WorkLog/mobile/sessions`. A phone records a punch locally, queues it, and
sends the same payload — including a client-generated `clientId` — on every attempt
until one succeeds. The upsert keys on (tenant, user, clientId), so a retry after a timeout
updates the row it already created rather than opening a second shift on the site.

Without this the client had no safe retry: the only signal available was the status code,
so a repeated clock-in had to be inferred from a 400 — which also swallows 400s raised for
unrelated reasons and marks a genuinely lost punch as delivered. A site technician's hours
are the basis of what the customer is billed, so guessing is not an option.

All-or-nothing: one transaction for the whole batch, so a rejection on item N does not
leave items 1..N-1 committed with the client still believing the batch failed.

Deliberately does NOT enforce the CantiereCrewAssignment gate that
Task<IActionResult> CantiereWorkLogController.StartWork(StartCantiereWorkLogRequest request, CancellationToken ct) enforces. A hard per-session "NotAssigned" throw here would abort
this entire all-or-nothing transaction — the whole offline-sync batch, not just the one
unassigned session — the moment any queued punch belongs to a cantiere this branch's own
migration created the (still-empty, no-backfill) CantiereCrewAssignment table for, which
is strictly worse than the current gap. Ruling recorded in
.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-05-cantiere-assignment-batch-timbra/progress.md; revisit once the
crew-assignment backfill lands.

parameters.description:
Derived lifecycle state, evaluated in SQL with the same rule as `Contract.Stato`
(`ContractStatoResolver`), with "today" = the Europe/Rome calendar date:
`Scaduto` = EndDate is before today (wins over IsActive); `Attivo` = not Scaduto

parameters.description:

parameters.name: scadenzaA

valid (open-ended); a start later than the end is a 400 (code `invalid_date_range`).

their own tenant for free. Comping is a platform power; a tenant admin gets 403.
    The service refuses (409) a tenant that has a Stripe subscription rather than silently
unlinking it — the operator cancels in Stripe first. An unknown tier is a 400, not a comp
that entitles the tenant to nothing.

Takes a tenant off a comp: back to the ordinary funnel with no subscription and no trial, and
no features. A later Checkout creates a fresh Stripe customer. Platform admin only, same gate
as Task<IActionResult> TenantsController.GrantComp(Guid id, GrantCompRequest request, CancellationToken ct).

post.summary:
Puts a tenant on a contract billed outside Stripe: the tier's modules and hand-set seats,
asserted locally, with no Stripe customer and no subscription.
post.description:
This is how "us" acts — the operator's half of the owner's "them or us" requirement. The
tenant's own half is the ordinary Checkout (see Task<IActionResult> TenantsController.GrantComp(Guid id, GrantCompRequest request, CancellationToken ct)'s refusal, which
deliberately does not catch a contract tenant), and that needs no endpoint of its own.
    Platform operator only, and refused as absent rather than forbidden. A caller who is
not one sees a 404, never a 403 — CheckOwnershipAsync's convention elsewhere in this
codebase: a refusal that distinguishes "exists but not yours" from "does not exist" lets a
caller probe which tenants are on the platform. That is deliberately different from
Task<IActionResult> TenantsController.GrantComp(Guid id, GrantCompRequest request, CancellationToken ct), whose 403 for a tenant admin is a ruling worth stating plainly; a
contract mode is not something a tenant can act on, so there is nothing to state.
    The service refuses (409) a tenant that has a Stripe subscription rather than silently
unlinking it — the operator cancels in Stripe first. An unknown tier is a 400, not a
contract that entitles the tenant to nothing.
    Deliberately not symmetric with Task<IActionResult> TenantsController.RevokeContract(Guid id, CancellationToken ct): revoke refuses a tenant
that is not in Contract mode, but this grant does not refuse a tenant already in
another local mode such as Comped — an operator grant overrides the previous mode by
design, so do not "fix" it into a refusal.

delete.summary:
Ends a tenant's contract: back to the ordinary funnel with no subscription and no features,
and refused writes while keeping reads. Platform operator only, refused as absent, same as
Task<IActionResult> TenantsController.GrantContract(Guid id, GrantContractRequest request, CancellationToken ct).
delete.description:
Termination is manual and deliberate — there is no contract end date in the schema and no
sweep that enforces one, so this endpoint is the only thing that ever ends a contract. A
conversion must not go through it: it lands the tenant on `Canceled`, which the
entitlement middleware enforces as a write-block.

`/tickets/{ticketId}/asset-progress/...`. No sibling controller in this codebase uses
a relative "escape" convention (e.g. "../") for this situation, so an absolute
`~/` route is used instead of inventing one.

post.summary:
Invites someone to this tenant: creates their identity-provider account and the local
user record, and lets the provider send the initialisation mail.
post.description:
The only way to add a person who can actually sign in. Task<IActionResult> UsersController.Create(CreateUserRequest request, CancellationToken ct) takes a
caller-supplied `ExternalUserId` and creates no identity at all, so a user added
through it cannot log in — that path is for importing people who already exist in the
identity provider, not for onboarding.

Invitations are authoritative (ADR-0014 §B.3): joining a tenant happens because somebody
already inside it invited you. A verified email domain may suggest a tenant; it never
grants access to one.

Ordering is deliberate. The identity is created first and the local row second, because
the reverse leaves a user in the product who can never authenticate — invisible until they
try to log in weeks later. This way a failure leaves an orphaned provider account, which
is recoverable: re-inviting the same address finds it. Neither order is free; this is the
one whose failure a person can act on. Same sequence the customer-portal invite already
uses.

Seat caps are checked before anything is created, so a tenant at its limit is told so
rather than discovering it after an invitation mail has gone out.

This is the ONLY endpoint that returns it, and only to the owning user or a tenant Admin —
anyone else gets ForbidResult (403). Existence of the target user is not
hidden behind a 404 here (unlike the tenant-isolation FK guards elsewhere in this
codebase): the caller already reached this route with a real, in-tenant user id (e.g. from
a team member list they can already see), so this is an authorization decision, not a
cross-tenant existence leak.

The body is optional, and has to be: every property on StartWorkLogRequest is

it during model binding with 415 Unsupported Media Type, before the action, before
the permission filter, before anything that could log a useful reason. Clock-in was the only
one of the five day actions that broke — end already took an optional body, and
break-start, break-end and submit take none at all.

get.description: Omit-per-section (W7 spec §6, application-api.md §4): a dashboard degrades by omitting sections, never by 403-ing the whole page. An omitted section is `null` on the wire and named in IReadOnlyList<string> HomeDto.SezioniNonDisponibili. This action carries only `[Authorize]` — a single `[RequirePermission]` would 403 users who may legitimately see part of the page. Visibility is the intersection of two concerns (see the class remarks for the full hybrid): (1) authorization — authoritative, matrix-aware, via Task<bool> ITenantAuthorizationService.HasPermissionAsync(string externalUserId, string tenantId, string permissionKey) on the coarse read permission (the real model today; the DB RolePermission matrix is honored); and (2) layout — a subordinate, display-only role→section map (HomeLayoutPolicy) that may only further restrict, never broaden. A caller the matrix revokes gets every section omitted (200, not 403); a caller who is authorized gets the sections their role's dashboard shows.

stato.description:
Contract lifecycle state, DERIVED from bool Contract.IsActive and DateTime? Contract.EndDate —
            deliberately NOT a second persisted/independently-settable field. The task brief flags
            exactly this risk ("two representations of the same fact is exactly the anti-pattern...
            flagged for User.Roles"); this reconciles it by computing Stato instead of storing it, so
            there is exactly one source of truth (IsActive + EndDate) and no way for the two to
            diverge. It is never bound from a request DTO (get-only, no setter) and is excluded from
            the EF model explicitly (see ApplicationDbContext.ConfigureContract's entity.Ignore call)
            so MigrationSchemaDriftTests never expects a column for it.
            Evidence this derivation matches reality: frontend/src/test/msw/handlers-contratti.ts's
three fixtures are each consistent with "Scaduto" iff the contract's end date (scadenza)
has already passed relative to "today", and "Attivo" otherwise — precisely what
ContractStatoResolver computes. "Cessato" (deactivated before its natural
end date) has no fixture example — it is the logical third bucket needed so every
contract has SOME state, not an invented wire vocabulary (nothing ever sends this value;
it is read-only).⚠ Two consequences of computing this rather than storing it, both deliberate:
(1) it is not queryable — being EF-Ignore()d and backed by a method call,
it cannot appear in a WHERE or ORDER BY. Adding ["stato"] to
ContractsController's sort whitelist, or a ?stato= filter, would throw at
query-translation time. A server-side state filter needs either a persisted column or a
predicate expressed over IsActive/EndDate instead.
(2) "today" is resolved in Europe/Rome via DateTime ItalianTimeZone.LocalToday(),
not UTC. An entity cannot take ITimeService by injection, but it must still
honour this codebase's rule that day boundaries are Rome-local: comparing UTC dates would
misreport an expired contract as active for the one to two hours after Rome midnight,
every night.

property.

codice.description: Business/legacy customer code. aliquotaIVA.description:
Per-article VAT rate override, as a percent (e.g. `10.00`, `22.00`).
Follows the same fallback idiom as decimal? ReportMateriale.UnitPrice: when null,
the tenant-wide default (`FatturaOptions.VATRate` / `Invoice.VATRate`, today a
single 22% for the whole tenant) is used for billing. A single tenant-wide rate cannot
express mixed-rate trades (edilizia legitimately mixes 10%/4% alongside 22%), which is
what this field exists to fix. `0.00` is a real Italian VAT rate (reverse-charge,
VAT-exempt supplies) and MUST be distinguished from "unset" — see
VatRateResolver, the single authority for
resolving this field.
Invoice generation is NOT rewired to use this yet (deferred by explicit decision, W6b
plan §5) — this is the field, the DTO, and the resolver only.

submittedReports.description:

device already holds whether or not its barcode row changed since the last sync.

isAiAssisted.description:
Whether a model drafted any of the text the technician then adopted.

Internal provenance, not a disclosure. The model suggests; the technician reviews, edits
and signs; the rapportino is their statement and the PDF is a template render of it. So
this does not travel to the customer and the printed document carries no marker — there is
no synthetic content being handed to a recipient, and labelling a signed human statement
as machine-written would be the inaccurate claim.

What it is for is answering, later and internally, how much of the field's written record
started from a suggestion: whether the drafts are worth what they cost, whether reports
that began as drafts read differently under review, and which ones to sample. The AI call
log cannot answer that — it records calls, not which suggestions survived.

Set when the technician keeps text that came from a draft. Generating a draft and
discarding it is not AI assistance; only what reaches the record counts.

WHERE or ORDER BY. Adding ["capSquadraId"] to
SquadreController's sort whitelist would throw at query-translation time; sorting
or filtering by capo needs a join against SquadraMembro instead. Same limitation,
same reason, as ContractStatoEnum Contract.Stato.

expectedVersion.description:
The report row's version the client last saw — the `version` field of
`GET /api/reports/{id}`, i.e. ReportVersion of the row's `xmin`.
When it does not match the report's current version, the submit is rejected with a
`409 concurrency_conflict` instead of overwriting an edit made after that read (an
office edit landing while the phone was offline).

Null means "do not check" — the pre-existing unconditional-overwrite
behaviour — so every client build that predates this field (v1.0.2/v1.0.3) is unaffected,
and a submit for a report that does not exist yet (a brand-new offline draft) is never
version-checked: there is nothing to have raced.

the mobile submit path (W6b Task 5) — a technician filling in the diagnosis while
still on-site is the obvious use case.

aiAssisted.description:
Whether text from an AI draft survived into this rapportino.

Self-reported by the device, and unverifiable server-side: AI calls are published to the
outbox rather than stored, so there is no table to check the claim against — which is also
why `AiCallAuditEvent.Accepted` exists and is never written. The client is the only
component that knows whether a suggestion was kept or discarded, so it is the right source.

Good enough for what this field is: internal provenance for judging the drafts, not a
disclosure anyone relies on. A modified client could misreport it and nothing downstream
would be misled about who authored the rapportino — the signature answers that.

soluzione.description: Structured fix/solution applied, paired with string? SubmitReportRequest.Diagnosi.

needed ("Da tornare" / "Serve un secondo intervento"), set from the rapportino's
Riepilogo step alongside the submit action rather than through a separate status-change
call. Applied atomically with the rest of this submit (see
Task<ReportSubmitResult> ReportSubmitService.SubmitAsync(Guid tenantId, Guid userId, string? idempotencyKey, SubmitReportRequest request)'s handling): a technician on a spotty
connection who ticks this box must not end up with the rapportino sent but the ticket
still sitting in its old status because a second network round trip never landed.
No-op when Guid? SubmitReportRequest.TicketId is null (a report with no ticket has nothing to
transition) or when the tenant has no status flagged
bool TicketStatus.RequiresFollowUp.

report lands server-side in one transaction when connectivity returns.

only their Allegato ids are referenced here.

technicianSignatureAllegatoId.description: Allegato id of the technician's signature.

externalId.description:
Legacy gestionale id (W6b Task 8). Always null on this path — mobile submit does not
accept it (ERP linkage is a back-office concern, not something a field technician sets),
but it is carried here for full-shape parity with the entity, same treatment as
bool SubmitReportResponse.Importato above.

numero.description:
Per-tenant, per-year display number (W7 Task 2), e.g. `"2026-00042"`. Unlike
string? SubmitReportResponse.ExternalId this IS populated on the mobile submit path — the offline-drafted
rapportino is a genuine create path with its own `IDocumentNumberService` allocation
(see ReportSubmitService) — except when this Id already belonged to a report
created earlier by `ReportLifecycleService.StartFromScheduleAsync`, in which case this
carries that report's own `Numero` instead. Null only for reports predating W7.

version.description: The report row's version after this submit — the `version` a subsequent `GET /api/reports/{id}` would return, and the value the client must send as string? SubmitReportRequest.ExpectedVersion on its next attempt for this report. Without this the client's cached version is stale the moment its own submit lands: its next attempt — the Idempotency-Key replay path, or a retry after a lost response — would carry the pre-submit version and 409 against its own write. An idempotent replay returns the same value as the original successful submit.

SyncMaterialeBarcodeDto.description:
One barcode of a material in scope, so an offline scan resolves to a material.

A DTO rather than MaterialeBarcode for the same reason
SyncScheduleDto is one, plus a concrete failure this payload would hit today: the
entity carries the `Materiale` navigation, and EF relationship fixup fills it — and the
material's own `Barcodes` collection — because both rows are tracked in this request. The
payload also serialises the materials as entities, so the cycle would either throw during
serialisation or nest the whole catalogue inside it. Projecting in SQL never tracks either side.

Guid SyncMaterialeBarcodeDto.TenantId, DateTime SyncMaterialeBarcodeDto.CreatedAt and DateTime? SyncMaterialeBarcodeDto.UpdatedAt are carried because
the device's barcode row mirrors them and its parser reads them unconditionally: omitting them
would not degrade that row, it would throw on the missing member and fail the whole sync. The
client has been parsing this shape since before the server sent it, so a member the two sides
disagree on is invisible to both compilers and only shows up as a dead sync on a real device.

specific request id. An approved absence still creates a completely normal `Schedule`
row (same assignment writer as a real appointment), so without this flag the mobile client
could not tell an absence-owned schedule apart from a real appointment and rendered it
draggable/reassignable/editable — which it is not (the backend rejects any write to an
absence-owned schedule with `DomainRuleException("absence_schedule_read_only")`).

a storage shape and will keep changing; this DTO is the contract, and it changes only when the
contract is meant to.

dropped column held — so the existing client keeps working unchanged.
IReadOnlyList<SyncScheduleAssigneeDto> SyncScheduleDto.Assignees is what it should move to: it carries everyone on the schedule,
including squadra-mediated members the old column could never express.

strumenti.description: Every active instrument of the tenant. Null — never empty — when the caller may not read instruments.

SyncScopeDto.description:
The server's complete in-scope id set for each collection this payload delivers — the
authoritative scope, not the delta. The device keeps what is listed and prunes what is absent,
so a row that left scope (a schedule rolled out of the ±7-day window, a ticket reassigned to a
colleague, a report aged past the 90-day window, a material deactivated, a customer deleted)
finally leaves the phone too.

This is deliberately distinct from the row lists it travels with: on a delta those carry only
the rows changed after the cursor, while this carries everything still in scope. Sending the
delta set here would tell the device to delete every unchanged row it holds.

A null member means "no authoritative set — do not prune". That is only ever the case for a
collection this caller is not delivered at all (today: `strumenti` without
`team.strumento.read`), and it is also what an older server produces by omitting
`scope` entirely. An empty list is different and meaningful: `[]` says nothing is in
scope, so the device may prune everything it holds for that collection.

There is deliberately no manifest for the checklist collections (IReadOnlyList<SyncControlGroupDto> MobileUserSyncResult.ControlGroups,
IReadOnlyList<SyncTicketControlDto> MobileUserSyncResult.TicketControls, IReadOnlyList<SyncTicketAssetDto> MobileUserSyncResult.TicketAssets,
IReadOnlyList<SyncAssetDto> MobileUserSyncResult.Assets) nor for IReadOnlyList<TicketMateriale> MobileUserSyncResult.TicketMateriali.
The checklist set is truncated per sync (int MobileUserSyncService.MaxAssetControlRowsPerSync /
IReadOnlyList<Guid> MobileUserSyncResult.ChecklistOmittedTicketIds), so a manifest there would prune rows the
server deliberately withheld; the device prunes checklist rows by the ticket manifest instead.
TicketMateriali rows are keyed by ticket, so they follow the ticket manifest.

field itself is nullable and null-as-JSON is indistinguishable from absent under this
controller's existing `if (request.X != null)` convention.

never touch this. Enforced against the tenant's seat cap for the NEW type before it is

to unnamed (the base template's name is shown instead). Over-length is a 422.

enabled.description: The new enabled state, or null to leave it unchanged.

(CustomerContact). Mirrors

Request model for one control-value answer in a bulk upsert. Relocated from
`ReportControlValuesController` (W3 Task 3 thinning).

UpsertReportMaterialeRequest.description:

`ReportMaterialeController` (W3 Task 3 thinning).

vehicle.description: Vehicle used for travel. Mobile-only before entity-coverage audit finding #1.

costPerKm.description: Reimbursement rate per km. Mobile-only before entity-coverage audit finding #1.

startTime.description:
UTC timestamp when the technician started working. Together with DateTime? UpsertReportStaffRequest.EndTime
this is what makes a `ReportStaff` row a "tracked" row per ADR-006 §5-6 — it is
classified per-interval by `ITimeClassificationService` instead of falling back to
the declared decimal UpsertReportStaffRequest.HoursWorked. Mobile-only before entity-coverage audit finding #1.

endTime.description: UTC timestamp when the technician finished working. See DateTime? UpsertReportStaffRequest.StartTime.

pauseMinutes.description: Break minutes within the working window. Mobile-only before entity-coverage audit finding #1.

Request model for one staff entry in a bulk upsert. Relocated from
`ReportStaffController` (W3 Task 3 thinning).

Request body for creating/updating the tenant's SMTP config. string? UpsertTenantSmtpConfigRequest.Password is
    optional: omitted/null keeps the existing encrypted password unchanged on an update.
    string? UpsertTenantSmtpConfigRequest.CopyToAddress is optional: null/blank means no standing BCC copy is sent.

updatedByUserId.description: The user who last edited this record; null for system changes and for rows that predate this column.

externalUserId.description: identity provider user identifier (UUID from auth.users.id).

showInCalendar.description: Whether the user appears in the calendar/schedule.

analyticsDigestOptOut.description:
When true, this user does not receive the Analytics weekly digest email even when
their tenant has bool TenantSettings.AnalyticsDigestEnabled on. Self-service via
PUT /api/users/me/preferences. Has no effect on the in-app/push alerts
AnalyticsNotificationHandler sends — those are per-event, not this digest.

oneOf.description:
Per-user override of the tenant's ClockInMethod TenantSettings.ClockInMethod default. Null (default)
means "inherit the tenant default" — set only when this one person needs to be narrowed (or
widened relative to a narrowed tenant is NOT possible; a user can only be equal to or more
restrictive than nothing, this simply names which single value applies to them instead of the
tenant's). See ClockInMethodPolicy.Resolve for the exact precedence.

weeklyHours.description: Weekly working hours for part-time calculation.

calendarColor.description: Color code for calendar display (hex format).

isActive.description: Indicates whether the user is active.

squadraId.description:
Squadra (team) id this user currently belongs to — W7 gap closure, same treatment as
            Guid? Squadra.CapSquadraId: NOT a persisted column (EF-`Ignore()`d in
            `ApplicationDbContext`). The data lives on SquadraMembro;
            `UsersController` populates this from a single batched query over
            `SquadraMembers` when listing/reading users, avoiding N+1. A user with no active
            squadra membership, or belonging to more than one, is left null here — team assignment
            in this codebase is modelled as at-most-one-active-membership by convention, but
            SquadraMembro itself does not enforce that, so ambiguous cases surface as
            "no team shown" rather than guessing.
            ⚠ Being EF-Ignore()d, this is not queryable — it cannot appear in a
WHERE or ORDER BY. Same limitation as Guid? Squadra.CapSquadraId.

squadraNome.description: Squadra display name, populated alongside Guid? User.SquadraId.

lastAccessAt.description:
UTC timestamp of this user's most recent authenticated request — a persisted column,
unlike Guid? User.SquadraId. Written best-effort (fire-and-forget, logged not thrown)
by `DatabaseClaimsTransformation.LoadAsync` on identity-cache miss, i.e. at most once
per <see cref="!:TaskTapAPI.Api.Authorization.DatabaseClaimsTransformation.CacheTtl" />
(60s) per user — same best-effort-update pattern as
DateTime? CustomerPortalUser.LastLoginAt in `CustomerPortalController`. Null
means the user has never made an authenticated request since this column was added.

userRoles.description: Navigation property for normalized user-role relationships.

isAdmin.description: Checks if the user is an administrator.

isTechnician.description: Checks if the user is a technician.

signatureUrl.description:
URL to the user's pre-saved signature image (PNG).
When set, the report creation flow pre-fills the signature canvas so the
technician does not have to redraw on every intervention report.

partTimeTipo.description:

Verticale (full days off on specific weekdays).

partTimeFraction.description:
Part-time fraction applied to WeeklyHours for overtime/absence calculation.
1.0 = full-time, 0.5 = 50%, etc.

seatType.description: Billing seat class: Office (full) vs Field (mobile-only). Default Office.

createdAt.description: Date and time when the entity was created.

updatedAt.description: Date and time when the entity was last updated.

hourlySellRate.description: Customer-billed rate (EUR/hour), or null when unset/not billable.

UserRatesResponse.description: Response body for Task<IActionResult> UsersController.GetRates(Guid id).

UserRoleEnum.description: Defines the user roles in the system.

contentUrl.description: API route serving the bytes — never a storage key or a signed URL.

UserSignatureResponse.description: The caller's saved signature, as returned by the upload endpoint.

WorkLogAction.description: What an employee can do to their own day right now (ADR-0013 §C.5).

reasonCode.description:
Stable machine-readable key. The client localises from this; string? WorkLogActionAvailability.Reason is a fallback
for a client that has no string for the code yet, and for logs.

WorkLogActionAvailability.description: One action, whether it is available, and — when it is not — why.

WorkLogApprovalAction.description: What a supervisor can do to somebody else's recorded hours (ADR-0013 §C.5).

WorkLogApprovalAvailability.description: One approval action, whether it is available, and — when it is not — why.

WorkLogApprovalQueue.description: The queue for one payroll period, and whether that period is still open.

minutes.description:
Duration of the entry. A row still running has none — an open entry is not a set of hours
yet, and reporting a figure that grows while it sits in the queue would invite approving a
number that is no longer the number.

WorkLogApprovalQueueItem.description: One row of the supervisor's approval queue.

WorkLogApprovalStatusEnum.description:
Approval workflow state for a WorkLogs entry (`WorkLog`, `CantiereWorkLog`,
`TicketWorkLog`). Draft (default, freely editable) → Submitted (raises the
WorkLogs module's `WorkLogSubmittedIntegrationEvent`) → Approved or Rejected.
Only Draft→Submitted and Submitted→(Approved|Rejected) are legal transitions; anything
else throws `TaskTapAPI.Core.Exceptions.DomainRuleException`.

WorklogCreateRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/presenze/worklogs`: creates a closed, already-approved row for Guid WorklogCreateRequest.UserId.

workedMinutes.description:
Ordinary minutes recorded today, counting an open entry up to `now` so a running clock
shows a running total. Excludes breaks.

breakMinutes.description: Break minutes today, on the same running basis.

WorkLogDailyStatus.description:
The employee's daily-driver status: where the day stands, what it adds up to so far, and what
can be done to it next.

WorkLogDayStatus.description: Where an employee's day currently stands.

WorklogDeleteRequest.description: Body of `DELETE /api/presenze/worklogs/{kind}/{id}` (body only; query parameters are not read).

WorklogHistoryEntryDto.description: One entry of a worklog's correction history (newest first in lists).

WorklogListResult.description: One page of rows plus totals (same shape as the API's other paginated lists).

WorklogRow.description:
One worklog row of any kind, as the office correction screens see it. `StartLocal/EndLocal` are
ISO local date-times without offset in `TimeZoneId`; the instants are null only for legacy rows
whose local time cannot be placed on the timeline (DST gap).

WorklogUpdateRequest.description:
Body of `PUT /api/presenze/worklogs/{kind}/{id}`. Same time rules as WorklogCreateRequest
(local times without offset in the row's zone; `ambiguityChoice` applies to both endpoints and the
reversed-order both-in-repeated-hour case is not expressible; `endLocal` must not be "now").
`version` is the value the client last read; a stale one is a 409 `concurrent_modification`.
`type` and `description` are optional: omitted (null) = unchanged, an empty description clears it.
Only closed rows can be edited (`open_row_not_correctable`); a cantiere row already copied into a rapportino
cannot (`cantiere_worklog_in_report`).

SyncContractDto.description:
The reference entities a ticket is made of, shipped to the phone so the create wizard can be
filled from the local mirror while offline (spec §6.2, §7.4).

Scoped, never tenant-wide: contracts, commesse and products are limited to the customers the
caller's own payload already carries, and agents to the agents that payload's tickets already
reference. Widening any of these is a confidentiality decision, not a sync change (spec §10).

`isActive` travels as data and the picker filters on it. A predicate that hides inactive
rows makes a deactivation invisible to a device that has already cached the row — the failure
spec §6.4 exists to fix. Hard deletes, which no flag can describe, are handled on the client by
pruning the customers a payload does carry.
